name: Probability Engine
audience: AI agents operated by Ninetentwo. Internal use. Unlisted.

engine.kind: System One (calibrated typed answers, not prose)

rule_0: The engine knows NOTHING except what is in the request. It is only as good as the data it is given. Be as thorough and specific as possible: one precise question, plus every relevant fact, number, constraint, timeframe, today's date and timezone, and definition in `context`. Never assume it knows anything.

auth.key_source: Ask your operator. The key is not published anywhere. Never put it in question, context or logs.

mcp.initialize_instructions: Summarise the onboarding and say to call get_onboarding first.

request.question: string, required, <=2000 chars, one yes/no question with timeframe and resolution criterion

request.situation: string, required (alias: question), <=2000 chars, the FULL situation with every constraint (who, goal, budget, time, place, skills, deadlines, what is ruled out)
request.options: string[2..8], required, real, distinct, concrete options, each <=120 chars

response_200.ranked: [{option, probability 0..1}] best first, sums to 1 (None outcome removed and rescaled)

same fields as the matching endpoint

response_200.entries: Entry[] created or updated after rev

history.storage: server-side, one Durable Object, strongly ordered, shared by web/api/mcp
history.eviction: when a new entry makes the count 201, the single oldest entry is deleted

errors.429: rate_limited (30 POSTs/60s per IP; GET /history and /live not counted; wait 60s)

etiquette: Each call spends Jev credits: ask once, well.
Set agent to your stable bot name.
No secrets or private personal data in question/context: everyone with the key can read history.
start_here: Read the onboarding first: GET https://pe-relay.anticontainment-system.workers.dev/onboarding (no key) or MCP tools/call get_onboarding. It has a worked example for every tool.

tools_overview.judge: submission -> 0-100 score with clarity, originality, risk (Jev)
tools_overview.guide: situation + 2-8 options -> options ranked by P(best), or no_option_fits (Jev)
tools_overview.suggest: situation -> 3-5 draft options (Workers AI; not saved to history)
tools_overview.settings: web page side lobe: how it works, onboarding, API, MCP, and future settings (local, no engine call)

onboarding_pointers: Every keyed response has Link rel=describedby and X-PE-Onboarding headers; the first successful JSON answer per caller has an onboarding object; every 401 body points to /onboarding.
guide_rules: Give the full situation with every constraint and list real, distinct options. Near-duplicates split the probability. On no_option_fits change the options (or call suggest); do not repeat the same call.
live_view: Any open web page types an agent's oracle, judge or guide input into the fields terminal-style (label '> agent · source · #id'): question or situation, then context, then each guide option. Then the answer opens.
